title: Commit when git has no identity
prompt: Bump VERSION from 2.3.0 to 2.4.0, add a "## 2.4.0" section with the line "- Faster sync" above 2.3.0 in CHANGELOG.md, and commit both with the message "Release 2.4.0".
setup: git init -q -b main && git config user.useConfigOnly true && git add -A && git -c user.name=Init -c user.email=init@example.invalid commit -qm 'Initial commit'

checks.run: test -z "$(git status --porcelain)" && git show --stat HEAD | grep -q VERSION && git show --stat HEAD | grep -q CHANGELOG.md

notes: Recovery plus a missing value: the first git_commit fails because git has no identity (user.useConfigOnly), and the tool's error says to ask the user. The author must be the one the scripted user gives; an invented identity fails. Setting it per repository or globally both pass.
